title: Singularity Spotter
creator: Dan McCreary
subject: Robot Kinematics
description: Bend the elbow of a two-link arm and watch the determinant fall, the condition number climb and the joint speeds grow as the arm straightens or folds. Then classify eight elbow angles as safe, near a singularity, or singular, from the size of sin(theta2). Used in Chapter 12.

educational.topic: Singular poses of a two-link arm and the determinant of the Jacobian
learningObjectives: Classify eight elbow angles of a two-link arm as safe, near a singularity, or singular, from the value of sin(theta2), with at least 7 of 8 correct on the first attempt

pedagogical.teachingStrategy: Watch a number change with a picture of a straightening arm, then sort angles by a rule on that number
keyQuestions: Why is a pose near a straight arm a problem, and not only the perfectly straight one?
Why is a folded arm singular too?
commonMisconceptions: Only a perfectly straight arm is a problem
A negative bend is different from a positive one
assessmentOpportunities: Eight committed classifications, one attempt each; 7 of 8 for mastery
